key_insight: A generalised mathematical model predicts particle-bed entrainment and cloud formation across rotorcraft, bathysphere, lunar-landing and dust-devil flows.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support CFD predictions of sediment or dust clouds that affect visibility and operations near particle-covered surfaces.
method: Define a measure of particle-cloud formation potential.
Adapt entrainment assumptions for swirl-free flows, gravity-sensitive rotorcraft flows and updrafts.
Outline integration into existing CFD software.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports predictive model derivations, including a critical cloud-initiation height for swirl-free cases, but provides no experimental validation or quantitative accuracy results.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy across environments remains to be validated, particularly where adapting the modelling assumptions changes the dominant physics.
paper_title: Bathyspheres, dust devils, lunar plumes and Martian drones: a generalised mathematical model for particle-fluid flow fields generated by static particle bed entrainment across macroscopic scales
